contract_verdicts.evidence: backend/src/ingest/mis-budget.parser.ts walks the workbook outline and records it as a per-batch snapshot carrying no amounts, each leaf keyed by identity rather than sheet row; shipped and sealed under statement-model (PR #30).

backend/src/mapping/mis-mapping-master.ts records a TAGGED target per entry - workbook leaf or the reserved unmapped-GL bucket - provisional with reasons, with the loader rejecting a triple claimed twice and ingest reporting drift rather than splitting a line (decision 0023).

backend/src/sql/sqlBuilder.ts full-outer-joins Budget and Actual at leaf grain, filtering actuals by the resolved triples before aggregating per decision 0017; the six pre-existing gated proofs still pass, which is decision 0022's promise that the (gl_code, month) relation was untouched.

backend/src/semantic/semanticLayer.ts registers the statement_relation domain and backend/src/db/migrate.ts seeds its report grant, making sqlBuilder's statement branch reachable; the projection emits the bounded LIMIT the validator mandates, so the query runs through SelectionExecutor's validate-explain-execute path.

backend/src/mis/mis-statement.service.ts reads the outline of the budget batch for the SELECTED PERIOD - active budget batches are one per period - and folds bottom-up so every parent is derived and the grand total foots in outline order.

The service issues the projection once per period block and merges by leaf key, returning a SINGLE block when the selected period is itself the FY-YTD; amounts stay exact paise until the presentation boundary.

The route preserves the outcome split - unauthorized refused, uncovered plant unresolvable - and carries the scope readout, per-row source presence and contributing batch ids, with the unmapped-GL line counted in the grand total.

contract/src/api.ts defines MisStatementNode, MisStatementMeasureBlock and the resolved/unresolvable union, with money as FixedScaleMoney - a template-literal decimal string constrained to two places - so paise cannot be lost to a JSON float.

frontend/src/features/mis/statement-view.tsx renders the tree INLINE below the selector at the workbook's natural depth in outline order, with the GL code blank for the unmapped-GL line whose glCode is null by contract. Verified live: 106 rows, three-level depth.

Parent rows display the route's derived subtotals rather than recomputing them - verified live, Vehicle Maintenance Rs 20,000 / Rs 26,500 footing its children Rs 18,000 + Rs 2,000 and Rs 22,500 + Rs 4,000.

Each block renders Budget, Roll-over (empty), Actual and %, headed with the spec's labels derived from the block's own range; money in Indian grouping rounded to the rupee for display only; zero NaN on the live page.

The two outcomes render distinctly branched on the response outcome, and the statement names its active period. Design metrics measured live against the prototype: eyebrow 10px / 2.2px tracking / JetBrains Mono, grand-total rule rgb(12,53,41).

backend/src/mis/mis-statement.controller.ts serves the export behind AuthGuard plus RequireAction('report') under the global CSRF guard, with typed Swagger, the allow-list entry, and Content-Disposition in main.ts's CORS exposedHeaders - proven live to be readable cross-origin.
The route calls the statement service once and branches before any header: a resolved request streams the canonical slug filename, an unresolvable one returns plain JSON with no file headers.

The writer receives that one payload and never re-queries or re-derives; a really-generated workbook was reopened and matched the payload, including derived subtotals, the grand total and the unmapped-GL line.

The reopened workbook is worksheet 'Financial MIS', 109 rows, merged header groups, preorder data with outline levels 0-3, a merged Grand Total row, 107 numeric cells and 0 strings in the Budget column, format rupee-hash-comma-zero, and headings derived to match the screen.
Text cells originating in the uploaded workbook are neutralised so a value beginning =, +, - or @ cannot reopen as a formula in an artifact people forward.

The Download Excel control sits in mis-statement-actions, NOT .mis-filter-bar - verified live - in the prototype's secondary treatment (white ground, emerald border and text, 34px, 6px), building its request from the resolved scope so a changed selector cannot yield a mismatched file.
frontend/src/lib/api.ts adds a binary path keeping cookie credentials, CSRF bootstrap and a counted one-shot 401 refresh, since post<T> ends in response.json() and cannot carry bytes.
Only the exact xlsx media type is saved; a 200 carrying JSON shows the notice and saves nothing; any other type takes the error path, so a corrupt file cannot reach the user.
The filename comes from the server's CORS-exposed Content-Disposition with a single fixed fallback, and the object URL is revoked - verified live, one created and one revoked per download.
A failure surfaces as one clear state with nothing left pending, the rule this view had to be corrected for once already.

reviewed_scope: backend/src/mis/ (statement and export routes, services, DTOs)
summary: The governed boundary holds across both new routes and the download. The statement and export routes sit behind AuthGuard plus RequireAction('report') under the global CSRF guard, and the statement branch now honours the selection's authorized measures and dimensions - it previously returned every financial measure regardless, which the review caught and which mattered because the executor authorizes per measure and dimension. Coverage and authorization stay strictly separate: an out-of-scope plant is refused while a plant the master does not cover returns the unresolvable outcome, so neither leaks through as the other. The download inherits the same grant rather than becoming a way around it, branches on the outcome BEFORE setting any header so a JSON body cannot be saved as a corrupt workbook, and neutralises text originating in the client's uploaded workbook against formula injection - the export is precisely the artifact people forward. The export writer is a required dependency, so a wiring mistake fails at startup rather than on a user's download. No credentials appear in the diff.
